fire: Confirm incident location and set up safety perimeter of at least 50 metres
Activate fire suppression — deploy engine and tanker units
Check for persons trapped; start rescue operations if confirmed
Notify GIDC/industrial authority if fire is in industrial premises
Establish water supply chain (hydrant or tanker relay)
Ventilate structure if possible; avoid opening windows in wind direction
Deploy hazmat team if chemical fire or unknown accelerant is suspected
Set up triage area for burn victims; alert trauma hospitals
Post fire watch for 30 minutes after suppression for re-ignition
File incident report and initiate investigation of cause
flood: Verify flood level with nearest gauge station or field observation
Issue immediate evacuation advisory for low-lying and riverside areas
Deploy boats and rescue teams to stranded residents
Open relief shelters (schools, community halls) and notify public
Coordinate with GWRDC for dam/barrage water release information
Block roads under water; redirect traffic with signage
Inspect drainage pumps; activate flood pumps at key stations
Alert hospitals to prepare for water-borne disease surge
Track Vishwamitri and Mahi river gauge levels every 30 min
Log displaced families and coordinate food/water distribution
road_accident: Secure the scene — deploy police to manage traffic and crowd
Check number of victims and call ambulances (1 per critical patient)
Apply first aid; do not move victims with suspected spinal injury
Alert nearest trauma hospital (SSG Hospital) with patient count
Clear debris from road to restore traffic within 30 min if safe
Collect witness accounts and document vehicle positions
Check for fuel leak or fire risk; keep sources of ignition away
Coordinate tow trucks for vehicle removal
Notify RTO and traffic police for FIR registration
Provide family notification support for critical victims
medical: Dispatch ambulance with paramedic to scene immediately
Start CPR if patient not breathing and pulse absent
Control bleeding with direct pressure; apply tourniquet if limb
Notify receiving hospital with patient condition and ETA
Manage crowd — keep bystanders back and scene accessible
Collect patient ID and next-of-kin information
Document presenting symptoms and time of onset
If mass casualty, activate MCI protocol and call additional units
Ensure safe handover to ER staff and complete transfer documentation
industrial_hazard: Declare exclusion zone — 100–500 m depending on hazard type
Identify the chemical/substance using site MSDS or placard
Deploy hazmat team in appropriate PPE; do not enter without protection
Notify GPCB (Gujarat Pollution Control Board) and factory management
Evacuate downwind residents; communicate shelter-in-place if evacuation not possible
Shut off source if safe to do so (valve, pipeline, reactor feed)
Establish decontamination corridor for affected workers
Alert toxicology unit at hospital for antidote preparation
Monitor air quality downwind with detection equipment
Document all exposed persons for medical follow-up
building_collapse: Establish incident command and safety officer role immediately
Conduct rapid assessment — number of floors, occupancy, hazards
Deploy USAR (Urban Search and Rescue) team with dogs and listening devices
Mark search sectors; coordinate systematic search room by room
Shut off utilities — gas, electricity — at street level
Establish casualty collection point with triage tags
Alert all hospitals for mass casualty reception
Prevent secondary collapse — shore up unstable sections before entry
Maintain communication with trapped survivors via voice/tapping
Document persons accounted for vs. missing; notify families
gas_leak: Evacuate building and immediate vicinity (50-metre radius minimum)
Do NOT use electrical switches, phones, or open flames near leak
Call gas utility (GGCL) emergency line to shut off supply
Ventilate the area — open windows and doors from outside if safe
Deploy gas detection equipment to verify extent of leak
Establish an ignition-free zone; no vehicles, no smoking
Alert fire brigade to stand by for potential ignition
Check for persons overcome by gas; provide fresh air and oxygen
Do not re-enter until gas levels confirmed safe by detection
Conduct post-clearance inspection before residents return
other: Verify the nature of the report — is this a genuine emergency?
Dispatch patrol unit for on-site assessment if uncertain
Log the report in the system with 'other' classification
Refer to appropriate city department if civic complaint
Advise caller on correct emergency channel if misdirected
Close incident if confirmed non-emergency after assessment
Document disposition and outcome in audit log
